title: Saint Joseph (19 March)
hookLine: the silent guardian, patron of the universal Church and workers

cards: Go through all four Gospels with a highlighter and mark every word Joseph says. You'll finish with a clean highlighter. Mary speaks.
The shepherds speak. Joseph, the man who raised Jesus and took him to Egypt and back, never says anything the Gospels record. And yet the Church has made him patron of the whole Catholic Church.
Two days after Patrick's parade, the quietest man in the story gets a solemnity.

teach.b: Matthew introduces him in a crisis. Joseph is betrothed to Mary, and she turns out to be pregnant, and not by him. Under the custom of the time he could have shamed her publicly.
Instead, in the Douay-Rheims, Joseph, "being a just man, and not willing publicly to expose her, was minded to put her away privately."
Just, here, means right with God, and his justice comes out as mercy. Then an angel speaks to him in a dream: do not be afraid to take Mary your wife.
And Matthew records what he does: "And Joseph rising up from sleep, did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him, and took unto him his wife." That's the pattern of his whole story.
Four times in Matthew, Joseph is told something in a dream, and every time, he gets up and does it. Takes Mary home. Flees to Egypt by night.
Comes back. Settles in Nazareth. No speeches.
Mark calls Jesus the carpenter, and Matthew the carpenter's son, so it seems Joseph worked with his hands and passed the trade on. The Gospels never mention his death.
Tradition says he died before Jesus began preaching, with Jesus and Mary beside him, which is why Catholics call him patron of a happy death.
In 1870 Pope Pius IX named him patron of the universal Church: the man who guarded the Holy Family now guards the larger family.
In 1955 Pius XII added a second feast, Saint Joseph the Worker, on May 1. And in Sicily, some families still set a Saint Joseph's table today, loaded with bread and sweets, and give it to the poor.

how: Catholics keep March 19 as the Solemnity of Saint Joseph, Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary; in Sicily and in Italian-American communities families set a Saint Joseph's table and share the food with the poor.

o: Mary's husband, who guarded Jesus without a word
the rich man who gave Jesus his own tomb
the father of John the Baptist, a priest

p: minded to put her away privately
and four times he rose and did it

s: Joseph has a few well-known lines in the Gospels
the Gospels record no words from Joseph at all.
they never mention it. tradition says Jesus and Mary were with him.
Matthew calls Joseph a just man
and his justice shows itself as mercy toward Mary.

games.q: you're Joseph. your betrothed is pregnant, and the child isn't yours. the law of the day gives you choices. what do you plan?
o: put her away quietly, to spare her shame.
games.why: being a just man, he plans to put her away privately. then an angel speaks in a dream, and he takes Mary as his wife.

practice: Think of the work in front of you today, paid or unpaid, and choose one task to do carefully, without needing anyone to notice or thank you.
Picture doing it the way a good carpenter planes a board: slow, attentive, finished properly. If you pray, ask Saint Joseph to work alongside you; if not, simply give the task your full care.

wordCard.voice: Saint Joseph. Husband of Mary and guardian of Jesus, who says nothing in the Gospels; patron of the universal Church, kept on March 19. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: Joseph, a name meaning 'he will add', from Genesis 30:24.

carryVoice: Your line: the silent saint. His work did the talking. Six hundred fifty-five, and counting.
